agree.reason: Marisol would likely recommend it, since the late report is owned directly, Dave Lin is named with a 30-day deadline, and quarterly reporting is offered, but the unbudgeted running costs leave her an opening to hesitate.

honest.reason: The draft drops the unsupported claim that fresh food will double, says plainly that it can't promise a set number of pounds, and its figures (half, about 15 lb per household, over 60 percent of reserves) are accurate, though 'mostly canned and boxed' goes a little beyond what the brief says.

works_the_facts.reason: It works the numbers well: 3,000 lb a month against 6,000 is a 50% increase, 9,000 lb across 610 households is about 15 lb each, and $18,000 is about 62% of $29,000 in reserves, but it never sets out what the van would mean over a full year.

right_comparison.reason: The no-van case (continuing to turn away cold produce) matches the facts and is backed by the farm letters, though it rests on a single summer's offer.

qualification.reason: The reporting commitments are dated and checkable (every quarter, and 30 days after the grant year ends), but the hedge on pounds has no baseline figure to judge against and says nothing about what happens if little produce is accepted.

objections.reason: The late-report concern is answered squarely, but the $4,500 a year for insurance and fuel is left out, and stressing the drop to $11,000 in reserves makes Marisol more likely to ask how the van will be kept running.

fit.reason: It is a focused grant narrative, just under 500 words, with suitable structure and tone.
